It can coordinate the seeing as another element in the prior conditional frame, and it can also be heard circumstantially, making the witnessing accompany the arrival of help. words.prose: {{ar:رَأَيْتَ}} ({{tr:ra'ayta}}) turns the divine event into witnessed evidence. The second-person ending places a single addressee at the camera point, while the object {{ar:ٱلنَّاسَ}} ({{tr:an-nāsa}}) and the state clause {{ar:يَدْخُلُونَ}} ({{tr:yadkhulūna}}) make the seen content a mass entry in progress. Its perfect form secures the seeing inside the conditional frame, but the imperfect action inside it remains unfolding. The Form I wording casts the addressee as one who receives perception rather than one who displays evidence to others. The root range keeps the sight from being flat optics: the scene is seen, recognized, and understood as the visible confirmation of what 110:1 announced. It also reverses the seeing-plus-dīn frame of denial in 107:1 into a scene of entry into dīn in 110:2, and the internal hamza gives the first content word a small audible arrest as connection turns into witness.

words.prose: {{ar:ٱلنَّاسَ}} ({{tr:an-nāsa}}) is the seen object, but it is not inert. Its accusative case makes the people what the addressee sees, while the following plural verb makes them the actors within the seen state. The definite collective gathers humanity into one public object before {{ar:يَدْخُلُونَ}} ({{tr:yadkhulūna}}) and {{ar:أَفْوَاجًۭا}} ({{tr:afwājan}}) unfold that unity into many entrants and groups. After the actorless event-frame of 110:1, this noun visibly populates the scene, and its relation to God's dīn makes the human-divine pairing a movement into order rather than a loose juxtaposition. The root-family pressure keeps the mass from becoming faceless: the entry is a social human return to relation, with sociability and perception more locally useful than any replacement by a forgetfulness derivation. The assimilated n-sound in the noun also joins the plural ending and final tanwīn, letting the collective motion be heard as well as seen.

words.prose: {{ar:يَدْخُلُونَ}} ({{tr:yadkhulūna}}) is the motion at the center of what is seen. As a state clause, it shows the people in the act of entering, not after entry has finished. Its active Form I surface gives the people visible agency, while the accepted passive variant keeps the theological pressure of being admitted in the apparatus without replacing the canonical reading. The same Form I surface foregrounds entry itself rather than a causative admission or reciprocal blending. The verb's ordinary threshold sense is redirected by {{ar:فِى دِينِ ٱللَّهِ}} ({{tr:fī dīni llāhi}}): the crossing is into an abstract divine order, not into a physical room, and not into the root's unrelated defect or intrusion branches. That makes a common entry root marked in this rare dīn-governed frame: the opening of 110:1 is realized as people crossing through in 110:2, and the observed entry then triggers the personal response commanded in 110:3. Even the compact consonant texture supports the threshold image with constriction and release.

words.prose: {{ar:فِى}} ({{tr:fī}}) is the hinge that makes the motion enter a domain. After {{ar:يَدْخُلُونَ}} ({{tr:yadkhulūna}}), it carries both directional and locative force: the people move into {{ar:دِينِ ٱللَّهِ}} ({{tr:dīni llāhi}}), and that dīn is imagined as an interior that can contain them. The choice is stronger than mere approach or surface contact; the destination arrives after the verb and resolves the motion into a bounded divine order. The long ī sound links the preposition into the governed domain phrase, and the collective location in God's dīn prepares the personal Lord relation that answers in 110:3.

words.prose: {{ar:دِينِ}} ({{tr:dīni}}) is the semantic center of the ayah's motion. It is governed by {{ar:فِى}} ({{tr:fī}}), so it becomes the domain entered, and it governs {{ar:ٱللَّهِ}} ({{tr:allāhi}}) in construct, so that domain is God's. The word therefore should not be flattened to a thin label: within this phrase it gathers order, submission, obligation, governance, and accountability into one destination, with debt-like obligation present as pressure rather than a reduction to one concrete debt. Its singular construct form gives one unified domain, while the people and final groups supply plurality on the entrant side. The construction also marks dīn inside a rare witness-entry cluster: denial of dīn in 107:1 is answered by entry into dīn here, and the familiar dīn-plus-God formula is specialized as an entered domain. The front-vowel cadence binds the preposition and domain before the divine genitive lands, and the movement from God's help in 110:1 to God's dīn in 110:2 prepares the turn toward the Lord relation in 110:3.

baseline_models.focus_anchor: The seeing verb governs a plural, ongoing act of entering, while the final cohort term distributes the people into successive groups.
baseline_models.mechanism: Direct perception, boundary crossing, obedience, and grouped succession combine into a process rather than a census: human cohorts are visibly passing from outside to inside an order of worship.

activation_trace.role: Supplies sensory or insightful witnessing and makes the transition an observed event.
Keeps the moving collectivity specifically human and publicly manifest.
Provides literal passage across a boundary into an interior.
Defines the entered domain functionally as worship, obedience, and submission.
Segments the influx into bands arriving one after another rather than isolated persons.

changed_reading.after: A witnessed and still-unfolding transfer carries successive human cohorts across a boundary into God's order of worship and obedience.

baseline_models.focus_anchor: The verse joins what can be seen with a verb whose inventory also opens onto the inner and secret.
baseline_models.mechanism: Visible appearance and sensory detection establish public ingress, but entering also creates an interior that sight does not automatically disclose. The scene therefore distinguishes observable inclusion from inward integration.

activation_trace.role: Foregrounds visible appearance and the surface available to an observer.
Contributes recognition through sight, sensation, or hearing as the public evidence.
Introduces an inward or secret dimension that is not exhausted by visible crossing.
Adds the social ambiguity of a newcomer mixing among established insiders.

changed_reading.before: Seeing the entrants certifies a completed inward transformation.
changed_reading.after: The verse certifies public boundary crossing while leaving inward integration open; visible membership and interior condition coexist without becoming identical.

baseline_models.focus_anchor: People enter in groups into a domain whose branches include customary practice and organized authority.
baseline_models.mechanism: Cohorts do not merely add private convictions. Newcomers mix with insiders, estrangement can become familiarity, and repeated practice places them within an ordered social world; the influx recomposes the community that receives it.

activation_trace.role: Supplies familiarity overcoming estrangement as a possible effect of incorporation.
Figures entrants as newcomers who mix into an existing people or affair.
Makes habitual practice, not a momentary declaration, part of the entered order.
Contributes the civic image of a place structured by authority and obedience.
Makes incorporation collective and serial, so each cohort changes the receiving whole.

changed_reading.after: The verse depicts serial social incorporation: formerly external groups become familiar participants in a practiced and organized order.

context_deltas.mechanism: The prior arrival and release of closure give the focus entry a causal prehistory. What is seen in 110:2 is not spontaneous crowd motion but the downstream passage made possible when a closed approach becomes traversable.

activation_trace.role: Supplies the arrival or occurrence that initiates the temporal threshold.
Supplies release of closure and widening of an entrance as the enabling condition.
Realizes the enabled condition as actual passage into the interior.
Shows the opened route being used serially by successive groups.

structural_cues: The conditional onset in 110:1 precedes the witnessed progressive action in 110:2.
Opening and entering form a cross-ayah threshold sequence.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies arrival, released closure, and ingress; I supply the arrow that the opening enables the entry. A live alternative is that opening names victory or judgment without specifying a spatial cause.

changed_reading.after: Groups traverse an access newly made possible; their visible ingress is the enacted consequence of an arrived opening.

context_deltas.mechanism: Aid is explicitly manifested before the crowd scene, and the same divine referent marks both the source of that aid and the destination's ownership. The people's movement remains real agency, but it is nested inside an event not possessed by either crowd or observer.

activation_trace.role: Contributes aid that also makes its result manifest, reframing what the observer sees.
Locates the antecedent aid in the same divine source toward whom worship is directed.
Marks the entered religious domain as belonging to the worshipped one rather than to the witness.
Makes the crowd's ingress evidence perceived by the witness, not an achievement authored by sight.

structural_cues: The divine name recurs as possessor of both the aid in 110:1 and the entered order in 110:2.
The observer is grammatically a witness while the people remain the entering subject.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies aid, repeated divine attribution, and witnessed entry; I infer that the crowd scene manifests aid and redistributes credit. Alternatively, aid may label only the prior event while human response remains the immediate cause of entry.

changed_reading.before: The crowd and its witness jointly own a human success.
changed_reading.after: Human cohorts genuinely enter, but their movement is seen as the manifestation of aid whose source and destination exceed both entrants and observer.

context_deltas.mechanism: Rain-like relief, water issuing from an outlet, a carried water supply, and a broad pass align into a material analogy: cohorts move through the opened terrain like released water finding channels. This sharpens succession into a cascading, distributed influx.

activation_trace.role: Supplies rain and relief as the initiating influx in the material analogy.
Supplies water bursting from its outlet as the release mechanism.
The non-dominant mapped root contributes carrying and delivering water to the observed cascade.
Anchors the analogy back to actual ingress rather than free-standing water imagery.
Contributes the broad gap or open stretch through which the influx can spread.

structural_cues: Release in 110:1 precedes plural progressive movement in 110:2.
The final accusative describes the manner of entry, allowing distributed flow to color how the movement is imagined.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies rain, an issuing outlet, water carriage, a broad pass, and ingress; I align them as a hydrological analogy for cohort movement. The ordinary alternatives—victory, opening, direct sight, and human groups—remain primary lexical readings.

changed_reading.before: The groups are a static plural count.
changed_reading.after: The groups form a released cascade, distributing through newly opened channels while remaining actual human cohorts entering the divine order.

context_deltas.mechanism: A highly visible mass event can become an occasion for display or self-credit. The following acts of exoneration and praise redirect the witness away from possessing the spectacle and toward a response that clears the divine source and assigns praiseworthiness beyond the observer.

activation_trace.role: Introduces the live danger that public visibility can be converted into performance before people.
Supplies exoneration and transcendence as a corrective to appropriating the visible success.
Supplies explicit praise rather than blame and directs the event's evaluation.
Makes self-credit through a received favor a diagnostic counterpressure within the praise response.

structural_cues: The imperative response follows immediately after the second-person act of seeing.
The witnessed multitude supplies an audience-like scene in which display and credit become structurally possible.

reader_a.activated_readings_md:
1. **Mass entry as the visible proof that the opening has worked.** Lexical evidence: `ر ء ي` B001, seeing by eye or insight; `ر ء ي` B012, showing/making seen; `د خ ل` B001, entering; `د ي ن` B001, obedience/religion; `ف و ج` B001, group after group; activated by `ف ت ح` B001/B006, opened aperture/key. Structural cue: 110:1 names opening; 110:2 gives sight, people, entering, dīn, and groups in one chain. Assigned role: vision verifies; people are the moving body; entry is the boundary-crossing; dīn is the interior domain; groups show repeated passage through the opened access. Abductive move: I infer that seeing is not incidental but evidentiary: the opened way is known by the traffic through it. Reading change: the ayah reads not just as "many people join," but as the empirical disclosure of a newly passable divine domain.

2. **Entering dīn as entering ordered authority, not only private belief.** Lexical evidence: `د ي ن` B001, obedience/submission/religion; `د ي ن` B006, city/place of ordered authority; `د ي ن` B002, reckoning/recompense; `ر ب ب` B001, lordship/ownership/authority; `ن ص ر` B001, aid that makes prevail; `ف ت ح` B003, judgment. Structural cue: 110:2 says "dīn of Allah" after "help of Allah"; 110:3 addresses "your Lord" and forgiveness. Assigned role: dīn is the governed order entered; lordship names the authority of that order; judgment/reckoning keeps entry from being merely social affiliation. Abductive move: I infer that collective entry into dīn creates a civic-juridical space with obligations and reckoning. Reading change: "في دين الله" reads as entering God's ordered jurisdiction, not merely adopting an identity label.

3. **The groups as waves, tributaries, or herds moving through opened space.** Lexical evidence: `ف و ج` B001, successive groups; `ف و ج` B002, wide opening/stretch; `ن ص ر` B007, tributary watercourses coming from afar; `ف ت ح` B005, water released from an opening; `د خ ل` B007, bringing camels back to water; `ن و س` B002, driving camels; `ر ب ب` B014, gathered herd. Structural cue: "أفواجا" sits at the end of the entry line, after the opening in 110:1 and before ritual regulation in 110:3. Assigned role: the branch network turns the groups into mobile batches, either water-like tributaries or pastoral bodies guided toward a trough/interior. Abductive move: I supply the movement-model that turns separate branch images into one process: opened access produces repeated incoming bodies needing guidance. Reading change: the ayah gains a kinetic texture; the people are not a static crowd but successive flows requiring channeling.

4. **Seeing the people also tests the danger of public display.** Lexical evidence: `ر ء ي` B005, showing off before people; `س م و` B008, good repute spread; `ح م د` B005, claiming praise by favor; `س ب ح` B002, declaring God free; `ح م د` B001, praise/thanks. Structural cue: 110:2 centers the addressee's seeing of people, then 110:3 immediately orders praise of the Lord and seeking forgiveness. Assigned role: the public spectacle activates the risk of reputational self-credit; tasbīḥ and ḥamd redirect the visible success away from the human observer. Abductive move: I infer a moral danger from the packet's sequence: seeing crowds after victory can convert divine help into human glory unless corrected. Reading change: "ورأيت الناس" is not neutral observation only; it becomes a temptation-point that requires the corrective worship of 110:3.

5. **Entry into the interior exposes the need for inward repair.** Lexical evidence: `د خ ل` B003, inner side/hidden interior; `د خ ل` B004, hidden defect/deceit; `غ ف ر` B001/B002, covering and forgiveness; `ت و ب` B003, calling to repent/return; `ر ب ب` B002, repair, nurture, completion. Structural cue: the line says people enter; the following line commands seeking forgiveness and names divine tawwāb. Assigned role: entry is not only admission into an interior but exposure of interiors; forgiveness covers defects; lordly nurture repairs what entry reveals. Abductive move: I infer that mass entry brings unprocessed inward states into the dīn, so the next action must be protective repair rather than celebration alone. Reading change: the ayah reads as a pastoral burden: new entrants bring hidden interiors that must be received, covered, and nurtured.
reader_a.retrospective_surprises_md: 110:3 most strongly changed this ayah: the command to seek forgiveness made the public sight of crowds feel ethically risky and pastorally demanding. The `د خ ل` hidden-interior branches became newly relevant only after `غ ف ر` and `ت و ب` appeared. 110:1 supplied the gate and water-release; 110:3 supplied the discipline that keeps the incoming waves from becoming spectacle or self-credit.

reader_a.activated_readings_md:
1. **The opening of `110:1` becomes a traversed threshold.** `يَدْخُلُونَ` directly anchors `د خ ل B001` (going into a place, time, or action), `دِينِ` anchors `د ي ن B001` (obedience, worship, and a followed way), and `أَفْوَاجًا` anchors `ف و ج B001` (successive human groups). Retrospectively, `ف ت ح B001` supplies the opened aperture, while `ف و ج B002` adds the image of a wide gap or stretch. Opening, entry, ordered interior, and repeated batches occupy distinct roles; I infer that the prior opening is the enabling threshold of the present ingress. The ayah thus reads as the actual traversal and social occupation of what `ٱلْفَتْحُ` opened, not merely as a headcount after victory.

2. **Visible entry does not exhaust the entrants' interior.** `رَأَيْتَ` anchors sensory perception in `ر ء ي B001`; `يَدْخُلُونَ` also activates `د خ ل B003` (hidden interior) and, more cautiously, `د خ ل B004` (an inward defect or deceit). The grammar makes the mass entry visible to the addressed witness, but `110:3` turns that witness toward `ٱسْتَغْفِرْهُ`; the packet therefore juxtaposes observable exterior and unobservable inward liability. I infer that the later command corrects any claim that sight settles the inner state of either entrants or observer. `وَرَأَيْتَ` is consequently bounded evidence: it certifies public movement while leaving inward condition open to divine forgiveness and review.

3. **The spectacle tests the ethics of seeing.** Beside direct sight (`ر ء ي B001`), `رَأَيْتَ` activates `ر ء ي B002` (reflective judgment) and the latent `ر ء ي B005` (acting to be seen by people). The striking proximity of `رَأَيْتَ ٱلنَّاسَ` to a public multitude makes ostentatious visibility a live counter-reading, while `سَبِّحْ بِحَمْدِ رَبِّكَ` redirects evaluation and praise. The text supplies the spectacle and the redirection; I infer that mass visibility can tempt the witness to make himself part of the display. Seeing therefore becomes a demand for disciplined judgment: the observer must read the event without performing ownership of it before the people.

4. **Entry is incorporation into accountable order.** `دِينِ` activates `د ي ن B001` (obedience/submission), `د ي ن B002` (reckoning and recompense), and `د ي ن B006` (a city or place of organized authority). `د خ ل B008` supplies interleaving of inner parts, while `ر ب ب B001` in the next ayah supplies lordship and obeyed authority. The movement is thus from separate batches toward an ordered, internally related body under a lord; I infer the social incorporation from the spatial entry and authority branches. Entering God's dīn reads not only as adopting a label but as coming under governance, mutual arrangement, and accountability.

5. **The people are presented as a moving plurality.** Because the packet assigns `ٱلنَّاسَ` to `ن و س`, the word can activate `ن و س B001` (swaying or oscillating movement), which is reinforced by `يَدْخُلُونَ` and successive `أَفْوَاجًا`. The prior `فَتْح` supplies an opening but does not state what propels each group; I infer only that the collective field is mobile and responsive, not that individual agency is absent. Exploratorily, `ٱلنَّاسَ` therefore reads less like a static category and more like a plurality set in wave-like motion through an opened route.
reader_a.retrospective_surprises_md: `110:3` produced the main correction: after a scene defined by what the addressee sees, `ٱسْتَغْفِرْهُ` exposes the limits of visible evidence and activates the hidden-interior range of `د خ ل B003-B004`. Its commanded praise also made the otherwise dormant ostentation branch `ر ء ي B005` newly visible, turning spectatorship into an ethical risk. Finally, `رَبِّكَ` sharpened `دِينِ` from affiliation into governed and nurtured order through `ر ب ب B001-B002`.

findings.text: Görülen toplu giriş, önceki açılmanın gerçekten geçilebilir bir yol oluşturduğunu kanıtlar; açılmanın ölçüsü ele geçirilen şey değil, o yoldan geçen insanlardır.
Dine giriş, yalnızca bir kimlik edinme değil, Allah'ın yönetimi altında birbirine bağlanan, yükümlülük ve hesap taşıyan düzenli bir yapıya katılma olarak belirir.
Görülen kalabalık, durağan bir kitle değil, açılmış yolda art arda ilerleyen hareketli dalgalar gibi belirir.
Grupların gelişi, suya yöneltilen sürüler gibi rehberlik ve bakım gerektiren toplu bir hareket olarak da çağrışır.
Dışarıdan görülen giriş, ne girenlerin ne de gören kişinin iç durumunu kesinleştirir; sonraki bağışlanma buyruğu, görünür başarının ardındaki kusur ve aldanma ihtimalini açık tutar.
Kalabalığı görmek, gören kişinin kendisini başarının gösterisine dönüştürme tehlikesini de doğurur; sonraki övgü buyruğu, değerlendirmeyi ve itibarı yeniden Allah'a yöneltir.
İçeri giren toplulukların görünmeyen kırılganlıkları da dinin içine taşınır; bu nedenle kitlesel giriş, kutlamanın yanında örtme, onarma ve yetiştirme sorumluluğu doğurur.

Görünür olma açıklaması adlandırma gerekçesidir; insan olmanın kurucu tanımı değildir. Evde kimsenin bulunmadığını bildiren kalıp ise dal çekirdeğine genellenemez ve yalnızca kendi sözcüksel biriminde korunmalıdır.

lexicalization_scope.note: Çıplak biçimlerdeki insan ve insan topluluğu anlamı dal çekirdeğidir; evde hiç kimse bulunmadığını anlatan kalıp ayrı tutulur ve çekirdeğe yeni bir genel anlam katmaz.

source_synthesis.common_summary: Toplu anlatım, içeride bulunan olumsuz kusuru ortak çekirdek sayar; soy ve akıldaki bozukluğu, işteki kuşkuyu, aldatmayı, gizli düşmanlığı, iç çürümeyi ve yiyecek zararını bu çekirdeğin farklı görünümleri olarak sıralar.

concept_map.definition: Develer su içtikten sonra yeniden su başına götürülür veya susuz develer içmekte olanların arasına katılarak ikinci kez içmeleri sağlanır. Bir kaynak anlatımı, sürünün bir kerede sıkışık biçimde suya sürülmesini de aynı düzenin başka bir yüzü sayar.

identity_judgment.rationale: Kaynak ifadesi eklemlerin birbirine geçmesini, sinir çevresinde toplanan eti, bir renge karışan başka renkleri ve iki bölge arasında veya ağaç köklerinde kalan tüy ile otu ortak bir iç içelik ve ara konum düzeninde toplar.

lexicalization_scope.note: Tanım yalın iç içelik ve ara konum dalını açıklar; özel kuş ve kap adlarını ya da kalıba bağlı başka kullanımları buraya taşımaz.

concept_map.definition: Parçalar birbirinin arasına girerek birleşir, bir ana bölüm çevresinde toplanır veya iki bölüm arasında yer alır. Bu düzen eklem, et, renk, tüy ve bitki örtüsü gibi farklı maddelerde görülebilir.

facets.statement: Bir parçanın başka parçaların arasına girmesi veya onlarla iç içe birleşmesi temel ilişkidir.
Eklemlerin birbirine geçmesi ve etin bir sinir üzerinde toplanması yapısal örneklerdir.
Bir ana rengin içinde başka renklerin dağınık biçimde bulunması görsel alandaki uzantıdır.
Kuşun sırtıyla karnı arasındaki tüyler ve ağaç kökleri arasına giren ot, ara konum örnekleridir.

source_synthesis.common_summary: Toplu kanıt, parçaların iç içe geçmesi ve arada yer alması düzenini eklem, sinir çevresindeki et, renk karışımı, kuş tüyleri ve ağaç köklerindeki ot üzerinden farklı maddi görünümlerle açıklar.

lexicalization_scope.note: Dal hem yalın biçimleri hem de belirli söz öbeklerini içerir; söz öbeklerine özgü hükümdarlık ve gerçek inanç yolu anlamları yalın biçimin bütün kullanımlarına yayılmaz.

identity_judgment.rationale: Kaynak ifadesinin doğrudan gösterdiği varlık kent veya büyük yerleşimdir. lexicalization_scope.note: Tanım, yalın eylem çekirdeğini türemiş eylem ve varlık adlarından ayırır; türemiş biçimlerin kapsamı yalın eylemin tamamına aktarılmaz.

facets.statement: Temel eylem, bir varlığa tapınmak ve kişinin kendini bu tapınmaya vermesidir.
Eylemden türeyen varlık anlamı, kendisine tapınılan varlığı veya tapınma konusu sayılan nesneyi gösterir.
Ettirgen kullanım, bir varlığı başkalarınca tapınılır duruma getirme veya öyle sunma işlemini bildirir.
Güneşe kimi topluluklarca tapınılması nedeniyle ona tapınılan varlık anlamındaki bir ad verilmesi, varlık anlamının tarihsel bir örneğidir.

branches.source_phrase_ar: أصل واحد وهو التعبد، فالإله الله تعالى لأنه معبود، وتأله الرجل إذا تعبد، والإلاهة الشمس سميت بذلك لأن قوما كانوا يعبدونها (maqayis)؛ التأله التعبد (ayn)؛ أله بالفتح إلاهة أي عبد عبادة، مألوه أي معبود، الآلهة الأصنام، التأليه التعبيد، التأله التنسك والتعبد (sihah)؛ لا يكون إلاها حتى يكون معبودا، معبوداتهم من الأصنام والأوثان آلهة، الإلاهة الشمس، وإلاهتك وعبادتك (tahdhib)؛ إله اسما لكل معبود، أله فلان يأله الآلهة عبد، فالإله على هذا هو المعبود (mufradat)
